answer: No single identity may earn more than 1174 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. Because the ferrous cap is applied per key at the wander settlement, the nectar audit exposes each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces each extra identity to stay small, which multiplies the fixed burns of running them while capping the upside of each. That is 16 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
